ignoreValues.reason: A slide deck, measured rather than asserted. /deck is eleven .slide sections, all position:absolute, with every non-current slide at opacity:0 and visibility:hidden - so 97% of the page's text (6,499 of 6,667 characters) is hidden at rest and the rule is a TRUE POSITIVE on its metric. What it infers from that is wrong here: it looks for copy a reveal animation never un-hid, and this is one slide showing at a time. Checked before waiving: zero focusable elements inside a non-current slide, so nothing off-screen can be tabbed into; deep links #2, #5, #9 and #11 each land on the right slide from a cold load; ArrowRight and the next button bring a slide to opacity 1 within the .34s transition; the counter tracks. qa/site.spec.ts asserts exactly one .slide.on, that both ends disable their button, that a hash deep link opens its slide, and that no pre block collapsed. This entry was a bare line in ignoreRules with no reason for two weeks, and it is the only error-severity finding this file suppresses - which is precisely the one that should have to say why. Scoped to /deck only.

Pixel sampler crossing a control's edge, not a real ratio. /app's primary buttons are stock on ink (about 13:1) and its secondary text is 9.1:1; the detector reads the rendered image, so a sample that straddles a dark button's anti-aliased boundary on a stock-sunk panel returns 3.2-4.4:1 and the reported colours are always blends that appear in no stylesheet (#5e635f on #bcbbb0 = ink at 59% over ink at 22% over stock-sunk). Re-measured 2026-09-11 off the computed DOM: eleven distinct foreground/background/size combinations inside #app, none below threshold, worst 5.42:1. Two detector runs against the same unchanged page reported different blends (#5e635f on #bcbbb0, then #5d635f on #bdbbb0), which is an unstable sample rather than a stylesheet pair. axe-core runs the WCAG colour-contrast rule against the DOM on this page in qa/a11y.spec.ts and reports it clean, and qa/a11y.spec.ts also asserts the busy state cannot be shown with opacity. Scoped to this page only.
